findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed multiple cheeses out of date marked and visibly molded. 
1. Sliced Cheddar(date marked July of 2026)
2. Sliced Provolone (date marked August of 2026)
3. Fresh Mozzarella (best by date April of 2026)
4. Shredded Mozzarella (opened and missing date marking)
5. Shredded Lettuce (opened and missing date marking)
All items were voluntarily discarded. Ensure staff are checking the coolers daily to discard any out of date food items.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed two knives stored in between the knife storage block and the wall. This crevice is not considered easily cleanable and therefore is not safe for utensil storage. Items were moved during the inspection. Ensure that all cooking utensils are stored in a clean, dry location.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the caulking of the mop sink to be damaged. PIC was made aware and work order has been placed. Ensure that all physical facilities are maintained and in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
The Certified Food Managers (CFMs) were unable to produce Allergen Awareness Training during today’s inspection. Discussed with CFMs, who stated they will be retaking the course, and emailing verification to the inspector. Ensure Allergen Awareness Training is renewed every 3 years and maintained on file during future inspections.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector tested dish machine (puck). Dish machine was ran several times, starting initially at 135F and going up to 152F. Discussed machine not reaching 160F with PIC. PIC immediately put in a service call for the dish machine. Ensure that only triple sink is used until dish machine can be serviced. Inspector will return 04/14/2025 to re-asses dish machine.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.111 Manual Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. If immersion in hot water is used for SANITIZING in a manual operation, the temperature of the water shall be maintained at 77°C (171°F) or above.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer at the dish machine is registering as zero parts per million of chlorine when tested with an indicator strip. The technician arrived and worked on the machine. The machine is now testing at 50ppm chlorine. The violation is considered corrected on site. 
Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitizers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on device and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The floor in the employee, women’s restroom near the kitchen is in gross disrepair. The floor is cracked in several places, the tile is broken revealing raw concrete and the floor drain appears to be elevated. Repair the floor by the next routine inspection.  
PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed an area around the dish machine and the back splash on the dirty dish side of the dish machine to be sealed with white tape. Seal these areas with silicone or a cleanable, durable material.
Also, the seal behind the tee/coffee machines and the cabinet next to the tea/coffee station is showing signs of disrepair. Clean, seal, repair or replace and seal the cabinet in this area.  
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Inspector observed the ice machine drop guard to be soiled. Ice level was taken down and drop guard cleaned and sanitized. Clean and sanitize the drop guard, as it is a food contact surface, on a regular basis to maintain it clean. The violation is considered corrected on site.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

Inspector observed a black can liner in the flour container. The flour was discarded out of an abundance of caution. Can liners will only be used with manufacturer verification that the can liners are also food grade or food safe. The violation is considered corrected on site. Provide food safe/food grade container for dry storage items.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Observed various portions of ham (approximately 15lbs at 48F), A Beef pot roast (10 lbs at 45F) soft mozzarella balls (10 lbs at 45F)  in the walk in cooler. These items were voluntarily discarded by the facility.  The outside thermometer of the walk in reads above 50F and the internal thermometer reads 42F. The cooler was recently repaired. The repair company is on site working on the unit again. All other items in the cooler were stored lower and when probed read between 40F and 44F. These items were moved to the walk in cooler unit outside which is holding food at 37F. Store all TCS foods at 41F or below.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. 

The outside thermometer of the kitchen walk in unit is observed to read above 50F. The independent internal thermometer located by the compressor reads 42F. The cooler was recently repaired. The repair company is on site working on the unit again. All other items in the cooler were stored lower and when probed read between 40F and 44F. These items were moved to the walk in cooler unit outside which is holding food at 37F. Watch unit to ensure that it is holding food at 41F or below.  A spot check will be conducted to verify that the unit repair is holding. Use outside walk in coolers until the unit is functioning properly.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

Observed soil and debris in the wait station base cabinets and along the tops edges of the cabinets at the white house. Also, fans not in use in the kitchen are observed to have soil.  Clean and maintain non food contact surfaces clean.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following non-food contact areas in need of cleaning:
1. Both large fans for air flow in the kitchen have an accumulation of dust.
2. The wall directly left next to the kitchen hand sink has food splash.
3. The spray nozzle before the dish machine area has a build-up of debris.
4. Shelving rack above 3 compartment sink has light layer of grime and dust (dish machine trays sit on this).

Ensure staff routinely cleans non-food contact surfaces. Discussed with PIC. Wash, rinse, sanitize. Clean before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

Observed no paper towels at the hand sink near the coffee server station by the kitchen. Discussed proper stocking of hand sinks with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.112: Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the PREMISES at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests. 

Observed dead roaches near the coffee server station by the kitchen. Ensure routine cleaning of dead pests.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following NonFOOD-contact areas to be in need of cleaning:
1. Spray nozzle of 3 compartment sink has build-up of debris and grime on top and under the nozzle.
2. Two large fans in kitchen have accumulation of dust.
3. Base of reach-in cooler has debris build-up.

Ensure to wash, rinse, and sanitize these areas before next routine inspection. These are repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 7/9/20.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Ice machine and walk-in cooler fans (food contact surfaces) are soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Observed baffle of ice machine to have an accumulation of mold and debris. Observed the outside walk-in cooler fan to have dust and debris. Discussed routine cleaning of food contact surfaces with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 7/20/20.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on multiple areas of facility. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Observed multiple areas of the facility to have soil residue present:
1. Spray nozzle of 3 compartment sink has build-up of debris and grime on top and under nozzle.
2. Fans throughout facility (above dish machine, two large floor fans) have accumulation of dust.
3. Food splash behind hand sink in kitchen and general area of this wall. 
4. Base of reach-in cooler has debris build-up.

Ensure routine cleaning of nonfood contact surfaces. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16  (C) Mop was found stored incorrectly in-between use. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.  Reference 6-501.16.

Observed mop to be within utility mop sink and not hanging in a manner that allows to drip dry and/or air dry. Discussed with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 12/20/2019.
findings.citation_text:
6-201.11  (C) Multiple areas were found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

Observed multiple areas of facility to be in a state of disrepair or no longer smooth and easily cleanable:
1. Caulking at kitchen hand sink, caulking of service station/coffee area, caulking of dish machine. Ensure re-caulking repairs are conducted before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec.. 3.07. Allergen awareness training.
(b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed CFPM to lack allergen training. Discussed certification with PIC. Provided paperwork with information. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 12/20/19.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-501.112  (C) Roaches observed, dead, in the corners near hand sink. The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate roaches, using proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.112.

Observed multiple dead roaches in the corners of the hand sink. Discussed disposing of pests with PIC.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on several items in breakfast area. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

Observed lack of date marking on several items within fridge of the breakfast area. Discussed importance of date marking and proper technique with PIC. Items within banquet area had appropriate date marking.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-204.11  (P) Bleach brand is not approved for use as a sanitizer. Chemical sanitizers must meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940, or meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020. Reference 7-204.11.

Observed bleach in breakfast kitchen to not have information regarding sanitization of food contact surfaces. Discussed appropriate bleach with PIC. PIC obtained correct bleach from banquet hall. COS.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204-112  (C) A thermometer is not provided in the kitchen refridgerator. Cold/Hot holding equipment used for Time/Temperature Control for Safety food shall have at least one thermometer in an easily viewed location. Reference 4-204-112.

Observed lack of thermometer in kitchen fridge at breakfast area. Discussed need for thermometers in all cold holding equipment with PIC.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-904.11  (C) Clean utensils are not protected from contamination at banquet kitchen. Clean utensils and single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food- and lip-contact surfaces are protected form contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

Observed plates in stacking equipment to not be covered in banquet area. Plates routinely have a cover and PIC replaced it during inspection. COS.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-501.110  (Pf) The wash water temperature is too low at 158.9 deg F in the mechanical warewashing machine that uses hot water to sanitize.  The temperature of the wash solution in spray type warewashers that use hot water to sanitize may not be less than: stationary single rack 165 deg F; stationary dual temperature machine 150 deg F;single tank conveyor with dual temperature 160 deg F; and multi-tank conveyor with multi-temperature 150 deg F. Reference 4-501.110.

Observed dish machine to register at 158.9°F with maximum registering disc after multiple attempts to run machine. PIC called dish repair service (MJ Kellner) during inspection. Dish machine must reach a minimum of 160°F. Follow-up will be conducted on 12/30/2019.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14.

Observed no maximizing register themometer for the dish machine that utilizes heat to sanitize. Discussed need for equipment with PIC in order to maintain appropriate temperatures of dish machine. Follow-up will be conducted on 12/30/2019.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16  (C) Mop was found stored incorrectly in-between use. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.  Reference 6-501.16.

Observed mops to be resting within utility mop sink. Mops must be stored in a manner that allows to drip dry and/or air dry when in-between uses. Discussed proper mop storage with PIC. COS.
findings.citation_text:
6-201.11  (C) Floors in the banquet coffee making area were found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

Observed several tiles to be missing in the corner of the banquet coffee making area, as well as missing coving. Discussed repairs with PIC.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

Observed breakfast staff to lack food handlers license. Discussed need for all food handlers to have appropriate licensing.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: PA 100-0367 (C) All CFPMs at a high risk facility should have completed an ANSI accredited allergen awareness program. Currently this has not taken place. Hand out were given to the PIC and they were instructed to ensure that all CFPMs complete an accredited course prior to the next routine inspection. This is a repeat violation for the 2019 inspection year.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: Facility does not have a certified food protection manager present during early breakfast hours. Kitchen staff is not reported to arrive until around 8 am and the breakfast staff arrives at 4 am. 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment: Observed employee chewing gum in food preparation areas at the breakfast bar. It was discussed that gum is not allowed in food prep areas and employee removed. 2-401.11  (C) Employee observed eating in the food preparation area. Provide designated area outside for eating. Reference 2-401.11.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment: Several live adult roaches are observed in the dish area of the kitchen. There is a corner to the left of the dish machine with caulk that is not smooth, and a couple adults were observed sitting in this area with one dead adult in the water on the table below. There was also a live adult on the dish machine itself. When looking through other areas near the kitchen, there is a large mechanical room where the hot water heaters are located that is warm and dark and numerous live adult roaches are observed in this room that is just off the kitchen. Adams Pest Control was reported to be here and treated on 7/11 and again this past Wednesday. A call was placed for pest control service at the time of the inspection and they should be here at some point today. 6-501.111  (Pf) The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate pests, using proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.111.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Breakfast bar area does not have test strips available for testing chlorine sanitizer concentration. Provide breakfast bar with chlorine test strips. Main kitchen has test strips and they will provide breakfast area with some until another set can be ordered for this area. Each area needs test strips with the color coded key to prepare to the correct concentration. 4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Chlorine dish machine found with 0 ppm chlorine sanitizer concentrations at the time of inspection. Chemical reservior bottle for chlorine found missing. Chemical siphoning apparatis which draws sanitizer into dish machine found submerged into floor drain beneath the dish machine. PIC indicated dish machine recently received maintenance repairs. A new chemical bottle was hooked up. Dish machine could not be verified having proper concentrations during inspection. PIC indicated maintenance would be done soon to repair dish machine. (Dish machine registered reaching 159.3F on the high temperature monitoring disk). 

Chlorine concentrations at 3 compartment sink measured with 0 ppm at the beginning of inspection. Chlorine reservoir bottle observed to be running low. New bottle was hooked up. Concentrations were verified to be between 50-200 ppm. 

->Sanitization logs to monitor concentrations were left with PIC. 

->Chlorine sanitizer concentrations must be maintained between 50ppm to 200ppm. Please use test strips to verify proper chlorine concentrations for adequate sanitization. Reference 4-501.114.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Employee beverage with lid and straw noted stored above container of dressing in 2 door upright cooler near the back door. PIC discarded beverage. 

->Food shall be protected from any potential contamination. Please store employee beverages in a manner to prevent contamination from food, food contact surfaces, or clean utensils.  Reference 3-307.11.
